package_info.package_versions: N/A (attack technique, not a package version)
package_info.why_malicious: Magecart is a digital skimming attack that injects malicious JavaScript into eCommerce checkout pages to steal customer payment and personal data, exfiltrating it to attacker-controlled domains. This code operates without merchant or customer consent, violating privacy and payment security.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into cart or checkout page JavaScript (client-side)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads payment form fields (card number, expiration date, CVV) from the checkout page DOM and sends this data via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain, resulting in payment data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code collects sensitive payment information from the DOM and transmits it to an external, non-payment processor domain, which is a classic sign of skimming.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal checkout page scripts should only transmit payment data to trusted payment processors, not to unknown or unauthorized domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment processors may collect form data, but only to trusted, documented endpoints.
key_indicators: Network requests to unrecognized external domains

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when customer loads any page with personal data forms)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into site-wide JavaScript or third-party scripts

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads personal data (email) and browser cookies, then sends this information via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled domain, enabling personal data leakage.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code exfiltrates personal data and session cookies to an unauthorized domain, which can be used for account takeover or further attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not transmit personal data or cookies to unknown third parties.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some analytics scripts collect user data, but only to trusted, privacy-compliant endpoints.
key_indicators: Access to personal data and cookies
Runs on sensitive pages (login, registration, checkout)

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is injected into the cart or checkout page (via compromised third-party or direct injection).
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimming/data leakage code in customer browsers.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code collects sensitive data (payment info, personal data, cookies) from the DOM as customers fill out forms.
attack_chain.leads_to: Preparation of stolen data for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Collected data is sent via network requests to attacker-controlled domains.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment and personal data.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript accessing payment or personal form fields on checkout/cart pages
Network requests from client-side scripts to non-payment processor, non-whitelisted domains
Exfiltration of data immediately after form submission
file_indicators: Unexpected or unauthorized JavaScript files loaded on checkout/cart pages
Changes in third-party script content or new script inclusions
network_indicators: POST requests to domains not associated with payment processors or analytics
Outbound traffic from checkout pages to unknown external endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor and scan client-side scripts on cart and checkout pages for unauthorized access to sensitive form fields and outbound network requests to unapproved domains. Review all third-party scripts for changes, and block or alert on any script that attempts to exfiltrate data to unknown endpoints. Regularly audit the domains present on sensitive pages and ensure only trusted payment and analytics providers are allowed.
